newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coal miners bike back into Bonn in triumph.
newsitem.headline: German coal miners bike back into Bonn in triumph.

text.p: German coal miners roared back into Bonn on their motorcycles on Thursday celebrating a deal with the government that avoided mass layoffs while Bonn cuts back its subsidies for their dying industry.

The pitworkers, who spent the night at a sports stadium in nearby Cologne awaiting news of the deal, had trade union flags fluttering from their bikes as they paraded down the boulevard they had blocked for three days.

Policemen who stood guard around government buildings during the blockade did the "Mexican wave" to the miners as they returned to hold a celebration rather than the protest they had threatened if the deal went against them.
Under the deal, Bonn pledged to avoid mass layoffs as it cuts back its subsidies from over nine billion marks now to 3.8 billion ($2.2 billion) in 2005.

The agreement means the miners to be laid off -- about half of the coal industry's 90,000-strong workforce -- will be offered early retirement and retraining schemes rather than being put directly on the dole.
Although the confrontation ended peacefully, Bonn police were ready for unrest if the talks had failed.
The headquarters of the liberal Free Democratic Party (FDP), which protesters had chained shut during the three-day blockade, was surrounded by police barriers.
Trucks full of officers, many of them young men and women who clearly sympathised with the plight of the miners, were also waiting along the Rhine River to be deployed if needed.
But the bikers roared through Bonn without stopping for another protest and later dispersed.
